summary: Frontend E2E of new auth features (forgot/reset in-app code + change-password modal) in Squawk King IA. All 6 scenarios passed. (1) Forgot flow: registered throwaway t1final_*@example.com, /login -> forgot-link -> forgot mode, POST /api/auth/forgot-password returned 6-digit code shown in reset-code-display AND prefilled into reset-code-input; entering new password + Update Password called POST /api/auth/reset-password, mode switched to login with auth-info 'Password updated. Sign in with your new password.', login with NEW password (brandNew789) succeeded (200, token stored in sk_token), login with OLD password (origpass123) rejected with 'Invalid email or password'. (2) Unknown-email (neverregistered_*@example.com): auth-error 'No account found with that email', reset-code-display NEVER rendered, stayed in forgot mode. (3) Change-password wrong-current: modal opens via key icon (change-password-btn), submitting current='wrongCurrentPw' -> change-password-error 'Current password is incorrect' (backend 400). (4) Change-password mismatch: new/confirm mismatch -> change-password-error 'New passwords do not match', /api/auth/change-password NOT called (network listener confirmed no request). (5) Change-password success + REVERT: squawk123 -> tempSquawk9! succeeded (modal closed, sonner toast 'Password changed successfully' present in DOM); then reopened modal and reverted tempSquawk9! -> squawk123 (verified post-run via curl /api/auth/login = 200). (6) Regression: mechanic@squawkking.io / squawk123 login OK, 3-pane workspace loaded (change-password-btn visible in sidebar). Skills loaded: none (auth-only UI wiring test, no AI capabilities exercised; ai-testing-core skill not required per its own definition since no LLM/image/audio surfaces were touched).
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx: after forgot-password success, the 'Reset code generated. Valid for 15 minutes.' auth-info banner persists into the reset step and can be mistaken by users (and by automated tests) for the outcome of the reset submission. Consider clearing setInfo('') at the start of the reset submit, or replacing the banner immediately on mode change so the current-step status is unambiguous.

Login.jsx line 43: reset-password error handling uses the same auth-error box; when the code is expired/used the message text depends on backend detail — verified 'No account found with that email' for unknown email is friendly, but consider explicit toast on reset success in addition to auth-info so the flow feels closed even if the banner is missed.

Login.jsx line 130: email input is disabled in reset mode (good — prevents changing the email between forgot and reset) but the visual disabled:opacity-60 is subtle; consider a lock icon so users know they can't edit.

ChangePasswordModal.jsx: no minimum-length client-side check on new password ('min 6 characters' shown as placeholder only). Backend presumably enforces it — if backend rejects short passwords the error surfaces via change-password-error, but a client-side guard would give faster feedback and match the placeholder promise.

ChangePasswordModal.jsx: success flow closes modal immediately after toast — good UX. But if the user was in the middle of another action, the abrupt close may be jarring. Consider a 300–500ms delay so the toast is clearly associated with the change-password action.

Login.jsx: reset code is displayed on screen (by design, no email delivery). This is fine for demo/in-app but should NOT be shipped to production without a rate-limit on /api/auth/forgot-password to prevent enumeration + brute-force of reset codes. Recommend server-side per-IP/per-email rate limiting.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All auth flows (login, register, forgot/reset in-app code, change-password) are UI-wired correctly. Selectors on /login: auth-form, auth-toggle, forgot-link, back-to-login, email-input, name-input, password-input, reset-code-input, reset-code-display, auth-info, auth-error, auth-submit. Change-password modal (opened via sidebar-footer data-testid=change-password-btn): change-password-modal, current-password-input, new-password-input, confirm-password-input, change-password-error, change-password-submit, change-password-close. Note: after forgot->reset the reset-code-input is auto-prefilled by React state, so tests do NOT need to re-type the code. Reset flow returns to mode=login on success (reset-code-display detaches; forgot-link becomes visible again). Client-side new/confirm mismatch check runs before any /api/auth/change-password network request (confirmed by request listener). Sonner toasts appear top-right for change-password success ('Password changed successfully').
